study_identification_part.si4_title: Detecting  accelerated  retinal  decline  in  mental  disorders through normative modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract explicitly states the use of normative modeling to estimate age-related retinal decline in healthy controls and to compare patients with SZ, BD, and MDD against this normative decline. It also states a priori hypotheses about accelerated decline and its expected gradient across disorders, and clarifies the purpose of applying normative modeling (individual-level comparisons rather than group averages). These satisfy the criteria (objectives and purpose of normative modeling).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "...we used normative modeling to estimate age-related decline of the human retina (and its expected variation) and compared it to the decline seen in schizophrenia (SZ), bipolar disorder (BD), and major depression (MDD). We hypothesized accelerated retinal decline in mental disorders compared to controls, with SZ being most affected, followed by BD, then MDD."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study builds a new normative model from UK Biobank healthy controls. Eligibility criteria are described: complete OCT imaging for all retinal metrics, inclusion of OCT image quality measures, and exclusion of diagnosed eye disorders. Image quality standards (UKBB OCT quality fields) are specified. The final sample size (N=56,545) is reported. Reasons for exclusion include eye disorders and data incompleteness, and an explicit outlier removal procedure (IQR trimming) is described to remove unreliable measurements without removing disease-related deviations.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text:
"we used these measurements from N = 56,545 healthy individuals from the UK Biobank who had complete OCT imaging data for all retinal metrics... including image quality control measurements (data fields 28552, 28553: OCT image quality) and without diagnosed eye disorders (data field 6148)." 
"outlier values were excluded using an interquartile range (IQR) trimming approach... Outlier removal was performed separately within the control population and each diagnostic group"

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates are explicitly modeled: sex and laterality-specific models are built; age effects are modeled using fractional polynomials to capture non-linearity; image quality and reported ethnic background are included as covariates. Multi-site harmonization is not applicable (single UK Biobank source).
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text:
"We built sex- and laterality-specific models for each metric..." 
"To model the effects of age... we used fractional polynomials... Image quality and reported ethnic background were also included as covariates..."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source for the reference cohort is clearly specified as the UK Biobank, with OCT acquisition and measurement procedures described and prior references cited.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "This analysis used cross-sectional measurements of optical coherence tomography (OCT) from the UK Biobank database..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data from an existing dataset (UK Biobank) are used; per guidance, answer NA for SECONDARY data.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described: automated retinal thickness analysis using Topcon custom software with dual-scale gradient segmentation of nine intraretinal boundaries; OCT image quality control fields are included; and an explicit outlier removal (IQR trimming) and QC approach are reported.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text:
"Automated analysis of retinal thickness was performed using custom software developed by Topcon... used dual-scale gradient information for rapid segmentation of nine intraretinal boundaries..." 
"including image quality control measurements (data fields 28552, 28553: OCT image quality)..." 
"outlier values were excluded using an interquartile range (IQR) trimming approach..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Internal validation is conducted via an 80-20 5-fold cross-validation framework to compare distributional families using mean squared error, and via permutation-based splits training on 80% of HC and testing on held-out 20% HC vs patients to guard against overfitting.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text:
"To select the appropriate distribution for our model, we compared the performance of several distributions, quantified by mean squared error, in an 80-20 5-fold cross validation framework..." 
"A random 80% sample of the HC population was chosen at each iteration to train the normative models... compared between the remaining 20% of the healthy control population and the patient population..."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No application of the normative model to an independent external healthy dataset beyond UK Biobank is described.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is clearly specified: GAMLSS in R is used to model non-linear effects and full distributions; models are sex- and laterality-specific; age is modeled with fractional polynomials; z-scores are computed using the fitted μ and σ. Software and version (R 4.3.0) are provided.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text:
"we used GAMLSS in R, a flexible statistical framework modeling non-linear relationships... We built sex- and laterality-specific models..." 
"To model the effects of age... we used fractional polynomials..." 
"Individual deviation scores (z-scores) ... using the ... pNO, qNO functions from gamlss in R." 
"All statistical analyses were carried out with the R-software version 4.3.0."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "we compared the performance of several distributions, quantified by mean squared error, in an 80-20 5-fold cross validation framework..."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cohorts are drawn from UK Biobank (SECONDARY data). Eligibility is described via ICD-10 primary/secondary diagnoses for SZ (F20), BD (F31), and MDD (F33). Sample sizes are reported. OCT image quality controls and the same QC/outlier procedures are applied, and individuals with diagnosed eye disorders are excluded.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "we then included N = 538 separate individuals from the UK Biobank with a mental disorder... including SZ (N = 171), BD (N = 265), and MDD (N = 102), according to ICD-10 primary or secondary diagnoses (F20, F31 and F33 respectively)."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation scores (z-scores) are defined and computed from the normative model parameters (μ, σ). The study defines and uses an extreme threshold (|z| > 1.96) to identify infranormal/supranormal values, and discusses clinical implications by comparing patient groups to the normative benchmark and reporting enrichments of extreme deviations.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text:
"Individual deviation scores (z-scores)... using the actual value and predicted μ and σ..." 
"for each of the HC, SZ, BP, MDD... we estimated the percentage of individuals above and below 1.96 standard deviations, representing extreme values (infranormal and supranormal variability)."
